clue.text: Event that sees people on fire?

definitions.text: Event that sees people on fire?

parts.words: Event that sees people on fire?
parts.note: to fire someone is to give them the sack, so people 'on fire' might be people in sacks, hopping along in a children's sports-day race

explanation.surface: A question about some alarming occasion where people are ablaze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On fire' seems to mean burning, but 'fire' is slang for dismiss, i.e. to sack; competitors in this school sports-day race stand in sacks and hop.
explanation.definitionFit: A sports-day contest in which runners hop along inside hessian bags is exactly a race run in sacks.

clue.text: Revolutionary incentive after prison support for rider

indicators.note: after puts the reversed incentive below the prison word

parts.note: stir is slang for prison

indicators.note: revolutionary means turned around, so the incentive word reads backwards

parts.note: a spur is a stimulus or incentive

explanation.surface: A radical inducement once released from jail, propping up a rider.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' seems political but signals the reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: These metal loops hanging from a saddle hold a horseman's feet, giving support while mounted.

clue.text: Drink firms on either side of America

indicators.note: on, in a down clue, puts the firms above the letter from America

parts.note: two firms are two companies, each abbreviated CO

indicators.note: America begins and ends with the same letter, so either side gives that one letter

explanation.surface: A beverage from companies on both coasts of the US.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot chocolate beverage made from powdered cacao is a familiar drink.

clue.text: Such a customer may be right, and argue about protecting Left

indicators.note: protecting means the shuffled letters surround the letter for left
about means the letters of argue are turned around into a new order

explanation.surface: The customer is always right, and quarrels when shielding the Left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be' is a link; 'about' makes EGUAR from ARGUE, and L goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A habitual patron who returns time and again is the kind of customer a shop knows well.

clue.text: Cold joint and a bit of fried potato

parts.note: C is the tap abbreviation for cold
the hip is a joint of the body

explanation.surface: A meal of cold meat with a little fried spud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joint' suggests a roast of meat but is a body joint.
explanation.definitionFit: In British usage a strip of deep-fried potato, a French fry, is called this.

clue.text: Province of person elected in Ireland

indicators.note: in places the elected member inside the name for Ireland

parts.note: Eire is the Irish-language name for Ireland
an MP, Member of Parliament, is elected by voters

explanation.surface: Asks for the constituency of someone voted in by the Irish electorate.
explanation.definitionFit: A province can mean a sphere of authority or domain, and an empire is a realm under one ruler's control.

clue.text: Swallow one cocktail

parts.note: a martin is a bird of the swallow family
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Knock back a single mixed drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swallow' looks like a verb about drinking but is the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Gin and vermouth served with an olive is a classic mixed drink.

clue.text: State one's trapped in the subcontinent

indicators.note: trapped in places one's inside the subcontinent

parts.note: India is the country commonly called the subcontinent
one's is written as ONES without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone declares they're stuck in South Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: The Southeast Asian archipelago is a sovereign country, a nation state.

clue.text: Improves objectives to support half of them

indicators.note: to support, in a down clue, puts the objectives beneath the half word
half of takes the latter two letters of the four-letter word them

parts.note: ends are aims or objectives

explanation.surface: Goals improve when they back half the group.
explanation.definitionFit: To amend a text, correcting its errors, is to make it better.

clue.text: Nameless doctor noticing ring

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the word noticing is rearranged

parts.note: a ring is round, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: An anonymous physician spots a ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctor' reads as a noun after 'Nameless', but it is a verb meaning tamper with, signalling the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone travelling under concealed identity is effectively anonymous, without their real name known.

clue.text: Compliant, seeing nothing crooked about finish

parts.note: nothing is zero, shaped like the letter O

indicators.note: about means the crooked word goes around the finish word

parts.note: bent means crooked or dishonest
to die is to finish or end

explanation.surface: Submissive, finding nothing dishonest about how it ends.
explanation.definitionFit: Willingly doing as one is told is to be dutiful and compliant.

clue.text: Saddle hybrid gelding must carry

indicators.note: the two words hybrid gelding carry the answer inside them, spanning the join

explanation.surface: A saddle the crossbred castrated horse has to bear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saddle' seems to be horse tack, but it is the definition in its mountain sense.
explanation.definitionFit: In hill country a saddle is a low crest linking two peaks, a type of elongated raised crest of land.

clue.text: In truth, bank will be occupied by a student

indicators.note: occupied by means the student and the letter A move inside the word for bank

parts.note: to bank on is to rely on
L is the learner plate abbreviation for a student or learner

explanation.surface: Truthfully, a learner will be taking over the riverside.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are adverbs of sincerity meaning genuinely or actually, as in 'it is, truly, the case'.

clue.text: Philosophical character lying in grass

indicators.note: lying in places the character inside the grass

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass of wetlands
a sign is a written character or symbol

explanation.surface: A thoughtful figure reclining in the grass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Philosophical' here means calmly accepting, not given to philosophy.
explanation.definitionFit: Being philosophical about a setback means accepting it calmly, the attitude of someone who has given up resisting.

clue.text: Worry about frayed hems and material

indicators.note: about means the worry word goes around the shuffled hems

parts.note: care means worry or concern

indicators.note: frayed means worn into disorder, so the letters of hems are rearranged

explanation.surface: Fretting about worn-out hems on some fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worry' could be a verb, but here it is the noun wrapping round the shuffled letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine soft wool from Kashmir goats is a luxury fabric.

clue.text: Dad's film as a pirate in trouble

definitions.note: read as 'Dad is'; the definition is Dad, with the 's as a link meaning is

indicators.note: in trouble means the letters of film as a pirate are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Father's movie in which he plays a buccaneer gets into difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dad's' looks possessive but stands for 'Dad is'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin term for the male head of a household is a formal or humorous word for a father.

clue.text: Close call at home — hates to lose cover

parts.note: to term something is to call or name it
in means at home

indicators.note: lose cover means the outside letters of hates are removed

explanation.surface: A near miss at home: someone hates losing protection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close call' reads as a near miss, but 'Close' is the definition and 'call' is TERM; 'to lose cover' strips H and S from HATES, leaving ATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To close something, such as a contract, is to bring it to an end.

clue.text: Monstrosities seeing English rose upset after word of agreement

indicators.note: after puts the shuffled rose below the agreeing word

parts.note: yes is the word used to agree

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters of rose are rearranged

explanation.surface: Hideous sights as an English rose is knocked over after someone says yes.
explanation.definitionFit: An ugly building or blot on the landscape is a sight that offends, a monstrosity.

clue.text: Thug with cash will be crude but effective

parts.note: a rough is a violent, rowdy person
and means together with
the ready, or readies, is slang for cash

explanation.surface: A hoodlum with money will be rough but get the job done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The ready' is British slang for available cash.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes something improvised and unpolished that nonetheless works well enough.

clue.text: A European chap importing universal balm

parts.note: un is the French for a, so a European's 'a'

indicators.note: importing means the chap takes the letter for universal inside

parts.note: a gent is a chap, a man
U is the film-rating abbreviation for universal

explanation.surface: A man from the Continent bringing in a cure-all ointment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A European' means the word for 'a' in a European language, here French UN.
explanation.definitionFit: A soothing ointment or salve rubbed on the skin is a balm.

clue.text: Withdraw from race, disheartened with deal

indicators.note: disheartened means the heart of race is removed, leaving its outside letters

parts.note: to treat with someone is to deal or negotiate with them

explanation.surface: Pull out of the contest, dispirited, with an agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' and 'with' are links; 'disheartened' leaves RE from RACE.
explanation.definitionFit: To pull back or fall back from a position is to withdraw.

clue.text: Coaster in trouble without a convoy

indicators.note: in trouble means the letters of coaster are thrown into disorder
without means the letter a is left out of the shuffled letters

explanation.surface: A coastal ship in difficulty sails without an accompanying convoy.
explanation.definitionFit: Both nouns mean a protective guard travelling alongside ships or people.

clue.text: Singular sort of English disease

parts.note: S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular

indicators.note: sort, as a verb, means rearrange, so the letters of English are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A peculiar variety of English illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Singular' looks like an adjective meaning odd but gives just S.
explanation.definitionFit: This painful viral rash, herpes zoster, is a reactivation of chickenpox and a recognised illness.

clue.text: Rubbish found in South American station

indicators.note: found in places the rubbish inside the South plus American letters

parts.note: S is the compass abbreviation for south
US, the United States, stands for American
tat is cheap, worthless junk

explanation.surface: Litter discovered at a railway station in South America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'station' here means rank or standing in society, not a stop on a line.
explanation.definitionFit: One's station in life is one's social position or rank.

clue.text: Trace container for example, on the way up

parts.note: a tin is a container

indicators.note: on the way up, in a down clue, means the abbreviation reads from bottom to top

explanation.surface: Tracking a container, for example, as it ascends.
explanation.definitionFit: A slight hint of colour or a faint suggestion is a trace.

clue.text: One's levy halved for land offshore

parts.note: one's is I plus S, as in I'S

indicators.note: halved keeps the first half of the four-letter word levy

explanation.surface: A personal tax cut by half for territory beyond the coast.
explanation.definitionFit: An island is a piece of land surrounded by sea, lying off the coast.

clue.text: Speak, and put a value on love

indicators.note: on means the valuing word is attached after the zero in this across answer

parts.note: love means zero in tennis scoring, shaped like the letter O
to rate something is to assess its worth

explanation.surface: Talk, and decide how much affection is worth.
explanation.definitionFit: To speak at length in a formal, pompous way is to hold forth or declaim.

clue.text: Initially expecting a more serious person from Boston, say

indicators.note: initially picks only the opening letter of expecting

parts.note: sterner means more severe or grave

explanation.surface: At first anticipating a graver character from Boston.
explanation.walkthrough: Boston is a city on the US east coast; 'say' marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A Bostonian lives in the eastern United States, so is an example of someone from that region.

clue.text: Number left in case of therapy …

indicators.note: in puts the word for left inside those outer letters
the case of a word is its outside, so its first and last letters are taken

parts.note: went means departed, left

explanation.surface: A number of people departed in the middle of treatment, the clue trailing off.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this clue to the next as one sentence; it plays no part in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A score is a figure, a cardinal number equal to two tens.

clue.text: … uneasy — others not so much

parts.note: the rest means the others
less means a smaller amount

explanation.surface: Continues the previous clue: patients left therapy feeling uneasy, others less so.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone fidgety and unable to settle is anxious or agitated, without ease.
